summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with suprapubic pain and discomfort around his chronic indwelling Foley catheter, consistent with a urinary tract infection. He was started on meropenem due to his history of multidrug-resistant organisms and underwent replacement of his catheter. Urine culture showed mixed flora suggestive of contamination, but treatment was continued with ciprofloxacin for a full 7-day course. A penile ulcer was noted, with a wound culture showing sparse MRSA, interpreted as colonization; it was managed with local wound care. His blood pressure was low during admission, prompting discontinuation of lisinopril, to be resumed outpatient. He remained stable for his comorbidities including CAD, diabetes, and chronic constipation, which was managed with an aggressive bowel regimen. He was discharged home with services, with follow-up scheduled in urology and primary care.
